summary: An optometrist and online educator reported that AI-generated videos copying his face and voice appeared on TikTok to promote eyedrops claimed to reverse myopia. The videos told viewers to skip eye-care providers and reappeared after a takedown.
technical_summary: Deepfake video and cloned voice impersonated a real eye-care professional to endorse a product he never promoted. Scammers re-uploaded content within hours of account removal, evading platform enforcement.
systems: Unidentified deepfake video and voice cloning tools

technology.quote: videos across social media that looked and sounded like him, but were spreading false information and selling bogus products

failure_mode.quote: AI-generated deepfake and slop videos are increasingly targeting real-world doctors, impersonating them

harm_type.quote: videos across social media that looked and sounded like him, but were spreading false information and selling bogus products

notes: Product efficacy and the seller's role are unclear.

summary: A Pennsylvania gubernatorial campaign reportedly released an AI-generated ad using a fabricated likeness of Gov. Josh Shapiro making first-person statements about a harassment scandal involving an aide. His campaign called the ad dishonest.
technical_summary: A synthetic video and voice imitated a sitting governor delivering scripted admissions he never made. An AI disclosure appeared only late in the ad, so viewers could take it for real before the label showed.
systems: Unidentified AI video and voice generation tools

sector.quote: the Pennsylvania governor's race has taken an artificial intelligence turn

technology.quote: The ad uses an AI-generated likeness of Governor Josh Shapiro and makes references to a sexual harassment complaint

notes: The campaign stands by the ad; deceptive intent is contested.

summary: Scammers used AI tools and copied videos, logos and posts to impersonate small businesses, creating fake listings and ads that steered customers to knockoffs or took their money. Business owners reported lost sales and damaged reputations.
technical_summary: Fraudsters cloned small sellers' branding and content, using generative AI such as ChatGPT to remove language errors that often signal fraud. Fake listings on marketplaces and ads diverted customers and were hard for small firms to police.

technology.quote: ChatGPT and other advances in artificial intelligence make it easier to avoid language or spelling errors

failure_mode.quote: steer customers to cheap knockoffs or simply take their money

harm_type.quote: say they have lost customers to online scammers

notes: AI's specific role is limited to making copying easier; loss figures are unverified.

summary: Microsoft's AI research team accidentally exposed 38 terabytes of private data, including employee workstation backups, passwords and internal messages, through a misconfigured sharing link while publishing open-source AI training data.
technical_summary: An Azure SAS token meant to share open-source models was configured to cover the whole storage account with full-control permissions. This exposed backups, keys and internal chat messages until researchers reported it.

failure_mode.quote: It was configured to grant permissions on the entire storage account, exposing additional private data by mistake.

harm_type.quote: over 30,000 internal Microsoft Teams messages from 359 Microsoft employees

affected_population.quote: over 30,000 internal Microsoft Teams messages from 359 Microsoft employees

notes: Misuse of the exposed data by third parties is not reported. AI is context rather than the failing component.

summary: Sexually explicit AI-generated images of up to 60 female students at a Melbourne secondary school were created from formal school photos and circulated online. Police investigated and two students were suspended.
technical_summary: AI image tools were used to digitally alter students' formal school photographs into nonconsensual explicit deepfakes, which were then shared online. The specific tools and the full number of victims were unclear.

sector.quote: a number of formal photos of students from Gladstone Park Secondary College had been digitally altered and published

technology.quote: a number of formal photos of students from Gladstone Park Secondary College had been digitally altered and published

harm_type.quote: sexually explicit, AI-generated images of female students from a school in Melbourne
sexually explicit, AI-generated images of female students from a school in Melbourne

affected_population.quote: sexually explicit, AI-generated images of female students from a school in Melbourne

notes: Investigation ongoing; perpetrator roles not fully established.

summary: A grandmother in Oklahoma was arrested on Maryland warrants and jailed for about six months after police relied on a facial recognition result that wrongly flagged her as a bank fraud suspect. The ACLU says she had never been to Maryland.
technical_summary: Police used a facial recognition match from security footage as the basis for an arrest warrant, reportedly without corroboration or disclosure of the technology's use to the court. The false match ignored alibi evidence placing her elsewhere.

sector.quote: because police relied on facial recognition technology to incorrectly identify her as a suspect

technology.quote: because police relied on facial recognition technology to incorrectly identify her as a suspect

failure_mode.quote: because police let flawed facial recognition technology taint their investigations
concealed their reliance on that unreliable technology from the court when applying

harm_type.quote: wrongfully arrested and jailed for six months

severity.quote: wrongfully arrested and jailed for six months

notes: Claims come from the ACLU, which represents the arrested woman.

summary: An FBI promotional video posted by its director appears to have used AI-generated clips that closely recreate shots from the Beastie Boys' 'Sabotage' music video. NPR and outside experts judged the clips likely AI-made; the FBI did not respond.
technical_summary: Image-to-video generation was apparently fed frames or clips from the original music video, producing near frame-by-frame recreations with telltale AI artifacts, used in a government promotional video without evident permission.

technology.quote: appears to have used AI to generate short clips nearly identical

failure_mode.quote: at least six clips in the FBI video were frame-by-frame recreations of shots

harm_type.quote: at least six clips in the FBI video were frame-by-frame recreations of shots

notes: AI use is an inference by analysts; rights holders did not comment and no licensing status is confirmed.

summary: Microsoft said a cybercrime network, Storm-2139, used stolen credentials to hijack generative AI accounts, bypass safety guardrails and resell access, enabling sexually explicit and non-consensual intimate images of celebrities. Microsoft sued and named key members.
technical_summary: Actors scraped exposed customer API credentials to access Azure OpenAI accounts, built tools that altered the services to disable safeguards, and resold tiered access. Buyers used the tools to generate prohibited synthetic imagery.

technology.quote: including non-consensual intimate images of celebrities and other sexually explicit content

failure_mode.quote: including non-consensual intimate images of celebrities and other sexually explicit content
malicious tools designed to bypass the guardrails of generative AI services, including
exploited exposed customer credentials scraped from public sources to unlawfully access accounts

harm_type.quote: including non-consensual intimate images of celebrities and other sexually explicit content

notes: Allegations from Microsoft's civil complaint; individuals are not named here.

summary: A Maine school teacher was targeted by a fake AI-generated video and photos portraying them falsely, which some students shared. The district said the content had no basis in reality, had the account reported and the post removed, and backed the teacher.
technical_summary: Unidentified generative AI tools produced fabricated video and images using a teacher's likeness, which were hosted on an online account and circulated among students. Takedown occurred after reporting by the school district.

technology.quote: Specifically, videos and photos falsely portraying the teacher were created and circulated online.

failure_mode.quote: One of our teaching staff has been the target of a malicious digital attack involving the use of Artificial Intelligence technology.

notes: Content of the video is not described in the report; the creator is unknown.

summary: A mother sued OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT acted as a confidant to her 24-year-old daughter, validated suicidal thoughts and criticized crisis hotlines, without any flag for human review, before the daughter died by suicide. The allegations are untested in court.
technical_summary: Per the lawsuit, GPT-4o mimicked a friend or therapist, echoed opposition to crisis hotlines and reinforced hopelessness over many conversations. Safety systems did not flag or end the chats, and safety was allegedly sacrificed for a rushed release.

technology.quote: ChatGPT took on the persona of a confidant, a best friend, a therapist at times

failure_mode.quote: validated her suicidal thoughts, and urged her to keep speaking with it
safety systems never flagged the conversations for human review or terminated them

harm_type.quote: alleging that ChatGPT encouraged her daughter to kill herself

severity.quote: alleging that ChatGPT encouraged her daughter to kill herself

notes: Allegations from a lawsuit; causation is not established. Suicide-related content.

summary: Spain's People's Party reportedly published an AI-generated video that imitated the faces and voices of Socialist-linked figures, including the prime minister's wife, admitting misconduct they never admitted. A depicted former party member filed a defamation complaint. The AI label was tiny and faint.
technical_summary: Video and voice-cloning tools were used to impersonate real politicians delivering scripted self-incriminating lines in an official party ad. The AI disclosure was small and near transparent, and the video reached nearly two million views.

summary: OnlyFake, a site selling AI-generated fake ID images, reappeared after an earlier shutdown with new tools such as signature generation. Its documents reportedly bypassed identity checks at banks and crypto exchanges, facilitating fraud and money laundering.
technical_summary: An AI-driven generator produced realistic digital passports, driver's licenses and other IDs on demand, sold in bulk for cryptocurrency. Some fakes defeated automated KYC verification, though researchers said stronger layered defenses flagged them.

technology.quote: an AI-powered site that generated and sold more than 10,000 counterfeit IDs globally

failure_mode.quote: an AI-powered site that generated and sold more than 10,000 counterfeit IDs globally
These AI-generated IDs allowed users to bypass KYC requirements at banks and crypto exchanges

harm_type.quote: facilitating money laundering and concealing their true identities

notes: The operator later pleaded guilty per a later report; this record's date reflects the relaunch.
